newsitem.title: USA: Fed rate decision fails to silence Senate critics.
newsitem.headline: Fed rate decision fails to silence Senate critics.

text.p: The decision by Federal Reserve policymakers Tuesday to leave interest rates unchanged did not silence lawmakers who have criticized not only its past decisions, but also its closed-door operations.

"The Fed is the last American dinosaur," said Sen. Byron Dorgan, a North Dakota Democrat, referring to the secret sessions of the Federal Open Market Committee, the minutes of which are kept secret for several weeks.
Sen. Jack Reed said keeping the minutes secret until after the committee's next meeting deprives the public of the ability to understand the reasoning behind policy decisions.
"I strongly encourage the Fed to provide greater disclosure by releasing its minutes following each meeting," the Rhode Island Democrat told reporters.

Several liberal Democratic senators, who joined other lawmakers in signing a letter recently that urged Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan not to raise interest rates, expressed relief at the committee's decision, but said they were frustrated by the anxiety that mounts before each meeting.
"I wish there was some way that we could work that out of our economic system," said Sen. Paul Sarbanes, a Maryland Democrat.

"I'd like to see a Fed that is made up of Fed members that do not give us anxiety attacks every single time they meet," said Dorgan. "We would like to see some people appointed to the Federal Reserve Board that will relieve some of that anxiety."
Reed said it was frustrating in the days and weeks leading up to the committee's meeting to feel as though the nation's economic expansion was threatened by a rise in rates.
"I would hope that they would develop a more robust policy toward economic growth," he said.
Sen. Tom Harkin said the Fed should direct monetary policy toward expanding economic growth, instead of keeping it under control in a preemptive effort to dampen inflation.
"We should launch a preemptive strike against slow growth," the Iowa Democrat said.
